abstract: Gametogenesis, the process of meiosis coupled to gamete formation, transforms diploid progenitor cells into haploid gametes through extensive cellular remodeling and rewiring of gene expression. Several stress-responsive transcription factors (TFs) are upregulated during gametogenesis, but whether the cellular mechanisms that handle environmental stress also support the success of this developmental process is largely unexplored. Here, we show that four stress-responsive TFs, Hsf1, Skn7, and the paralogs Msn2 and Msn4, are endogenously active during budding yeast gametogenesis in the absence of external stress and drive distinct gene expression programs. Simultaneous meiotic depletion of Msn2, Msn4, and Skn7 compromise the fitness of the resulting gametes. We identified just two TF-dependent targets, the antioxidant genes TSA1 and AHP1, as important for gamete fitness, directly connecting TF activity to the protection of meiotic progeny. Our results demonstrate that the activation of canonical stress-response regulators is built into the meiotic program and suggest that such pathways can be repurposed during development to safeguard cellular health.
